en.name: Salsa, homemade fresh
en.summary: Home-made fresh salsa keeps 5–7 days in the refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F) — though freezing turns it into a cooking sauce rather than a fresh dip.
en.pantry: Home-made salsa is raw, so washing the vegetables properly before chopping is the only control step the recipe has. Lime juice and salt help and chilli does a little, but none of it amounts to a heat process, and there is nothing afterwards to correct a problem. Chill it as soon as it is made. Out of the fridge give it two hours at most, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F), and serve it from a small bowl set in ice at a barbecue rather than leaving the whole batch out in the sun.
en.fridge: 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, covered, on a cold shelf. The flavour actually improves over the first day as the onion and chilli settle into the tomato, then the tomato begins to break down and the salsa loosens. Liquid gathering at the bottom is normal; pour it off or stir it through. Use a clean spoon each time, never return salsa from the table to the container, and add fresh coriander and a squeeze of lime to lift a batch that has been sitting a few days.
en.freezer: 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Be clear about what you get back: freezing ruptures the cell walls of the raw tomato and onion, so it thaws soft and watery and is no longer a fresh dip. Drained and reduced in a pan it makes an excellent cooking sauce — for eggs, braises or rice — so freeze it in meal-sized portions with that use in mind. Leave headspace in the container, because it expands.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, drain off the liquid, and cook it down in a pan. Do not expect it to serve as fresh salsa. Never thaw it on the counter.
spoilage: A fizzy taste or a yeasty smell — it is fermenting.
Bubbles rising in the container, or a lid that has domed.
A slimy or ropy texture in the liquid.
Mould on the surface, or a dull brown colour through the whole batch.
tips: Wash the vegetables thoroughly before chopping; it is the only control step.
Serve from a small bowl and keep the container in the fridge.
Freeze in meal-sized portions, leaving headspace for expansion.
Refresh a few-day-old batch with new coriander and lime.

faq.q: How long does homemade salsa keep?
faq.a: 5–7 days in a covered container in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
Yes, 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F). It thaws soft and watery, so use it as a cooking sauce rather than as a fresh dip.

faq.q: Why has my salsa gone watery?
faq.a: Salt draws water out of the tomato and onion. Pour it off or stir it in. A watery salsa that smells clean is not spoiled.

zh.name: 自製新鮮莎莎醬
zh.summary: 自製的新鮮莎莎醬冷藏 4 °C 以下可放 5～7 天，冷凍 −18 °C 下 12 個月——只是冷凍會把它從「沾醬」變成「煮醬」。
zh.pantry: 自製莎莎醬是生的，所以「切之前把蔬菜洗乾淨」是整份食譜唯一的控制步驟。萊姆汁和鹽有幫助、辣椒也有一點，但這些都不等於加熱殺菌，而且後面沒有任何步驟能補救問題。做好立刻冷藏。離開冰箱最多兩小時，氣溫超過 32 °C 時最多一小時；烤肉時請分到架在冰上的小碗，不要整盆放在太陽下。
zh.fridge: 加蓋放 4 °C 以下 5～7 天，放冷藏層架。第一天味道其實會更好，洋蔥與辣椒慢慢融進番茄裡；之後番茄開始出水、整體變稀。底部積水是正常的，倒掉或拌勻都行。每次都用乾淨的湯匙，上過桌的絕對不要倒回容器；放了幾天的一批，補一點新鮮香菜和擠一點萊姆就會提起來。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 12 個月。但要先說清楚你會拿回什麼：冷凍會撐破生番茄與洋蔥的細胞壁，解凍後又軟又水，不再是新鮮沾醬。瀝乾後下鍋收一下，它會是很好的煮醬——配蛋、燉菜或拌飯都行——所以請以這個用途為前提，分成一餐的份量冷凍。容器要留膨脹空間。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，倒掉滲出的水，再下鍋收乾。不要期待它還能當新鮮莎莎醬用。不要放室溫退冰。
spoilage: 吃起來有氣泡感或聞起來有酵母味——它在發酵。
容器裡不斷冒泡，或盒蓋鼓起。
表面長霉，或整批變成暗褐色。
tips: 切之前把蔬菜徹底洗淨，那是唯一的控制步驟。
分到小碗上桌，容器留在冰箱。
分成一餐份冷凍，容器要留膨脹空間。
放幾天的莎莎醬，補新鮮香菜與萊姆就會回神。

faq.q: 自製莎莎醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 加蓋容器放 4 °C 以下冷藏 5～7 天。

faq.q: 自製莎莎醬可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，−18 °C 下 12 個月。解凍後又軟又水，請當成煮醬使用，不要當沾醬。

faq.q: 莎莎醬怎麼變得水水的？
faq.a: 鹽把番茄和洋蔥的水拉出來了。倒掉或拌勻即可；只要聞起來乾淨就沒壞。
